summary: Reports on the ARPANET Users Interest Working Group, a new group that grew out of a Boston meeting in May 1973 after BBN's Resource Sharing Workshop. The meeting served as a forum for users to air complaints, swap information and make proposals.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 585 reports on a meeting where ARPANET users discussed how to make network services easier to find and use. It records a wide range of concerns and lists specific work the group planned next.

subtitle: Notes from a meeting about making the ARPANET easier to use.

tldr.problem: The meeting sought a fuller account of the network issues that affected users and practical proposals for addressing them.
tldr.mechanism: Participants in the ARPANET Users Interest Working Group listed and discussed concerns about documentation, command interfaces, performance, feedback, messages, accounts and other user services.
tldr.outcome: The report records the concerns and assigns follow-up work on a new-user packet, a common command-language protocol and a standard editor.

today: RFC 585 records the concerns and planned activities discussed at an ARPANET Users Interest Working Group meeting.

sections.title: Purpose of the USING Meeting
sections.content: The ARPANET Users Interest Working Group (USING) grew out of a meeting in Boston on May 22–23, 1973, after BBN's Resource Sharing Workshop. The meeting gave network users a place to share complaints and information, express needs and propose user-oriented network capabilities. The group aimed to represent users, promote resource sharing, improve support and consider standardization.
sections.plainLanguage: The meeting gave network users a forum to raise problems and suggest improvements. USING aimed to carry those concerns into work on network services and interfaces.

sections.title: Issues Raised by Users
sections.content:
The participants compiled 13 categories of concern. These included clearer and better organized documentation, a common command language, site-performance information, ways to give feedback, useful error messages, interfaces for different experience levels, personal information management, accounting, trial access, prelogon services, remote-user assistance, moving information between sites and shared network utilities.

The recommendations included searchable online help, a new-user packet, tutorials, a network-wide information service, a common way to submit complaints and clearer diagnostics. The RFC notes that time did not permit full discussion of every topic.
sections.plainLanguage: Participants discussed many parts of the user experience, from readable help to simpler commands and better ways to report problems. They also raised ideas for training, account support and moving information between sites.

sections.title: Assigned Work and Next Steps
sections.content: The report assigns follow-up tasks: draft USING's goals, design a New User's Packet, prepare preliminary specifications for a Network Common Command Language Protocol, and specify a simple standard editor called NETED. It also proposes forming a general USERS group open to interested people and says the group's activities would be reported in ARPANET News.
sections.plainLanguage: The group assigned people to develop a new-user guide, shared command language and simple editor. It also planned an open USERS forum and further reports on its activities.
